newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Thousands in pro-peace rally in Jerusalem.
newsitem.headline: Thousands in pro-peace rally in Jerusalem.

text.p: Thousands of Israelis formed a five-km (three-mile)-long human "chain of peace" from downtown Jerusalem to the grave of assassinated Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin on Saturday.
The Peace Now group, which organised the torch-lit demonstration, ended the night-time memorial with a rally outside the office of right-wing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
"Bibi, resign. We don't want you anymore," the crowd shouted, using Netanyahu's nickname.
A politically divided Israel marked this week the Hebrew calendar anniversary of the November 4 assassination of Rabin by a right-wing Jew opposed to his peace policies with the Palestinians.
"I am here because of peace. We want peace with the Arabs," said eight-year-old Yaniv who marched with his parents and sister Michal, aged six, who said: "For me, Rabin was like a father."
Other Israelis played out their political differences in the streets.
One woman demonstrator, angered by heckling from another woman, hit her over the head with an Israeli flag.
"You should be ashamed of yourself," the heckler shouted.
"Keep it up and you'll see what you get," the flag-holder retorted.
Hundreds of candles lit Rabin's gravesite on Jerusalem's Mount Herzl, where family, friends and Israel's political leaders had gathered on Thursday for a state ceremony.

Police said about 1,000 paramilitary border policemen guarded the route to the cemetery from Zion Square -- where several weeks before the assassination right-wing demonstrators held posters depicting "traitor" Rabin in a Nazi uniform.

At the square on Saturday, a man was arrested after he burned a picture of the late prime minister, police said. Elsewhere along the route two religious Jews who shouted curses at demonstrators were detained.
"In the footsteps of Rabin, in the path of peace," read the posters on Saturday.
Some of the people in the chain wore stickers that said: "Friend, you are missed."
Peace Now estimated the crowd at 50,000. But not everyone saw the demonstration as a protest against Netanyahu and his rejection of Rabin's policy of trading occupied Arab land for peace.
"We see this as an expression of unity but it is nothing against the government," said Zvi Bandel, 64.
"I think you have to give (the government) a chance, you really do," said his wife Eva, 54.

Netanyahu's government is locked in U.S.-brokered negotiations with the PLO on implementing a long-delayed Israeli troop redeployment from the West Bank town of Hebron. Negotiators were expected to resume talks late on Saturday.
Earlier in Gaza, Palestinians held a memorial rally of their own -- to mark the first anniversary of the assassination of Fathi Shqaqi, leader of the militant Islamic Jihad group.
His killers were never found but Israel's Mossad secret service is widely believed to be behind the shooting.

In a message read at the Gaza rally, Shqaqi's successor Ramadan Abdallah Shallah wrote: "The Israeli enemy should not forget for a minute that all the world knows that all of Palestine is ours. We will not concede a single metre."
